name: Macedonian Tavče Gravče
description: Tavče gravče, North Macedonia's real national dish, literally means 'beans in a pan' - real technique boils the beans first, then makes a real separate roux of oil and paprika cooked together until fragrant, stirs this into the beans, and bakes the whole thing in a clay dish until a genuine crust forms on top; skipping the bake and stopping at a stovetop bean stew misses the entire point of the dish's name.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Cowpeas (blackeyes), immature seeds, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt

ingredients.ingredient: Cowpeas (blackeyes), immature seeds, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt

steps_detailed: Simmer the beans in enough water to cover, 15-18 minutes, until nearly tender.
Separately, warm the oil and whisk in the paprika, cooking briefly, 30 seconds, until fragrant - real technique makes this a genuine roux, not just a spice dusted on top.
Stir the paprika roux into the beans.
Transfer to a small baking dish, top with the onion slices, and bake at 400F (200C) for 25-30 minutes, until a real crust forms on top.
Scatter the fresh mint over just before serving.

name: Macedonian Ajvar
description: Ajvar, a roasted red pepper and eggplant relish, reaches its most celebrated form in North Macedonia, where whole towns roast peppers by the sackful each autumn - real technique roasts both vegetables until the skins char fully for genuine smoky depth.
steps_detailed: Roast the bell pepper and eggplant at 450F (230C) for 25-30 minutes, turning once, until the skins are fully charred and blistered.
Let cool slightly, then peel off the skins.
Blend or mash with the garlic, olive oil, and vinegar until mostly smooth but still a little textured.

name: Macedonian Šopska Salata
description: Šopska salata, Macedonia's real village salad, is genuinely built on ripe tomatoes and real grated cheese falling as a light, fluffy blanket over the top, real technique using a box grater rather than crumbling the cheese by hand.
steps_detailed: Toss the tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, and onion with the olive oil.
Grate the feta directly over the top, so it falls in light, fluffy shreds forming a real blanket over the vegetables.

name: Macedonian Kjofte
description: Kjofte, grilled meat patties, shares real roots with the wider Balkan and Turkish kebap tradition, real technique kneading the meat well and resting it before shaping.
steps_detailed: Mix the beef with the onion, cumin, and garlic, and let rest 15 minutes.
Grill or pan-sear, 4-5 minutes per side, until well charred and cooked through.

name: Macedonian Grilled Fish
description: Grilled fish rubbed with garlic and lemon, reflecting North Macedonia's Lake Ohrid and Lake Prespa fishing tradition.
steps_detailed: Rub the fish with the garlic and lemon juice, and let sit 10 minutes.
Grill or broil, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.

name: Macedonian Roasted Walnuts
description: A simple roasted walnut snack, common across North Macedonia.
steps_detailed: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring often, 4-5 minutes, until fragrant.

name: Macedonian Beef and Vegetable Stew
description: A simple, hearty beef and vegetable stew, common Macedonian home cooking outside the specific named dishes.
steps_detailed: Brown the beef with the onion, 8-9 minutes.
Add the carrot, potato, and tomatoes, and simmer 30-35 minutes until tender.

name: Macedonian Yogurt Garlic Sauce
description: A simple garlic-yogurt sauce, common across North Macedonia and the wider Balkans, served alongside grilled meat.
steps_detailed: Whisk everything together and chill before serving.
